title: Scope and Automatic Cleanup
goal: Understand how Rust automatically drops values when they go out of scope.

sections.text: In languages with a garbage collector, memory cleanup happens in the background. In C++, destructors run when objects go out of scope. Rust uses a similar automatic mechanism called dropping.

sections.caption: Scope braces define the exact lifetime of a value.

sections.text: When a variable goes out of scope, Rust calls its cleanup logic automatically. You do not write explicit calls to free memory or close handles.
Local variables inside the same block are dropped in reverse order of declaration. The last variable created is the first variable dropped.

sections.caption: Cleanup proceeds from bottom to top within a block.

sections.text: Manual early cleanup is done with `std::mem::drop`, which takes ownership and forces immediate drop at that line.

explanation: Understand how Rust automatically drops values when they go out of scope.
